code.note: client-only Vue SPA; all endpoints live on the out-of-repo backend

findings.title: Backend API serves customer PII with no authentication
findings.description: GET /api/ServiceOrders returns 1.6MB of customer records (fullName, contactNumber, emailAddress, address, accountNumber) with no token, cookie, or credential. Writes (POST /api/Naps) return 400 validation, not 401 — also unauthenticated.
findings.exploit_scenario: Anyone who can reach the IP runs curl -k https://103.249.198.50:8090/api/ServiceOrders and downloads the whole subscriber database; POSTs create/alter records at will.
findings.impact: Full read/write of all customer PII and network records. Data-protection liability.
findings.recommendation: Enforce auth server-side on every /api route. The backend already ships a token system (/api/Token, /validate, /revoke) — require and verify it.

findings.title: Stored/DOM XSS via unescaped Leaflet tooltip on the dashboard map
findings.description: Location name/address from the API were interpolated raw into bindTooltip(); Leaflet renders string tooltip content via node.innerHTML (leaflet-src.js:10034). Combined with the unauthenticated write API, an attacker-supplied location name executes in an admin's browser. Sibling LcpNapMap.vue already escaped; DashboardMapCard did not.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker POSTs a NAP/location whose name is . Any admin opening the dashboard and hovering the pin runs the payload, which exfiltrates the localStorage session object.
findings.impact: Arbitrary JS in an authenticated admin session; session/PII theft.
findings.recommendation: Escape all API-derived tooltip content (fixed this run; escapeHtml added, mirrors LcpNapMap.vue).
findings.verification: VERIFIED — traced innerHTML sink in Leaflet, confirmed open write API; fixed + regression test added

findings.title: Backend reachable only over TLS with an untrusted cert on a bare IP
findings.description: vercel.json and vite proxy target https://103.249.198.50:8090. curl rejects the cert (unable to get local issuer); -k succeeds. A bare IP cannot carry a valid public CA cert, and vite dev sets secure:false. Plain http on 8090 is refused (connection reset), so it is HTTPS-with-bad-cert, not cleartext.
findings.exploit_scenario: If the Vercel edge does not verify the upstream cert, an on-path attacker between edge and origin can MITM all API traffic (all customer PII). If it does verify, production API calls fail.
findings.impact: MITM of all API traffic, or broken prod.
findings.recommendation: Put the backend behind a hostname with a valid CA certificate and verify it end to end. Do not ship secure:false beyond dev.

findings.title: Client trusts a forgeable localStorage session; backend token flow unused
findings.description: isAuthenticated is true whenever localStorage.user has id>0 or a username. No bearer token is required or sent (the request interceptor attaches one only if present, and login stores none because the API returns none to this client). The backend exposes /api/Token but the frontend never uses it.
findings.exploit_scenario: A user runs localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify({id:1,accesslevel_id:1})) and gets a full Super Admin UI. Because the API (finding 1) enforces nothing, every action then succeeds.
findings.impact: Trivial client-side auth bypass; compounds finding 1.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the backend token flow: issue a token at login, send it as Bearer, verify server-side, and base isAuthenticated on a validated token, not a local object.
findings.verification: VERIFIED via code + live login probe (401 on bad creds, but no token issued)

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy on either deploy path
findings.description: vercel.json and nginx.conf set X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy (and Vercel sets HSTS), but neither defines a Content-Security-Policy. An admin app with a live XSS sink (finding 2) has no second layer to blunt injection.
findings.exploit_scenario: Any future XSS (or finding 2 before its fix) can load remote script and exfiltrate freely with no CSP to block the connection.
findings.impact: No defense-in-depth against script injection / data exfiltration.
findings.recommendation: Add a CSP (default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' the API + nominatim + tile hosts; img-src 'self' data: tile hosts; script-src 'self'). Note Vercel and nginx both need it; nginx.conf currently omits HSTS too.

findings.title: xlsx (SheetJS) 0.18.5 has prototype-pollution + ReDoS advisories, no fix
findings.description: Direct dep xlsx@* has GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6 (prototype pollution) and GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9 (ReDoS), no npm fix available. In this app xlsx is used only for export (XLSX.utils.json_to_sheet / writeFile) over API data — the vulnerable parse/read path is never fed untrusted input, so real risk is low today.
findings.exploit_scenario: Would require feeding attacker-controlled spreadsheet bytes to XLSX.read — no such path exists here. Risk becomes real if an import feature is added.
findings.impact: Latent; low until an import path exists.
findings.recommendation: Move to the maintained SheetJS distribution (cdn.sheetjs.com) or a smaller export-only lib (e.g. write-excel-file). Never call XLSX.read on user files without sanitizing.
findings.verification: VERIFIED — xlsx imported only at DynamicApiTable.vue:2356, write path only

findings.title: Build/transitive deps with advisories: postcss, nanoid, dompurify
findings.description: npm audit reports high postcss (via vite / vue-router compiler) and nanoid, plus moderate dompurify (via jspdf). All are build-time or bundled-transitive; postcss/nanoid have fixes via npm audit fix. dompurify is pulled by jspdf and only runs during PDF export.
findings.exploit_scenario: postcss/nanoid run at build, not in the shipped runtime path an attacker reaches. dompurify processes export HTML the app itself generates.
findings.impact: Low runtime exposure; worth clearing to keep the audit clean.
findings.recommendation: Run npm audit fix for postcss/nanoid; bump jspdf when a dompurify-patched release is out. Re-run npm audit after.
